chunks: And in the narration of Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
Regarding a man who comes to Dhā al-Ḥulayfah or some of the mawāqīt after salat al-ʿaṣr or at a time other than the time of salat.
He said: “He does not wait until the hour in which salat is performed. He only said that out of fear of notoriety.”

key_terms.ذَا ٱلْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, a known miqat for entering ihram
key_terms.مَخَافَةَ ٱلشُّهْرَةِ: out of fear of becoming publicly conspicuous
key_terms.ٱلْأَوْقَاتِ: the appointed miqats or designated stations/times referred to in context

ai.seo_question: If someone reaches Dhū al-Ḥulayfah or another miqat after ʿAṣr or outside prayer time, must he wait before entering ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning entering ihram at the miqat when one arrives after the usual prayer time or outside prayer time. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that one need not wait for a prayer time, and explains that the earlier instruction was due only to concern about attracting public notice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2564 - In a narration from Ibn Faddal, from Abu al-Hasan (as), regarding a man who arrives at Dhu al-Hulayfah or one of the Miqats after the Asr prayer or outside the time of prayer.

Imam (as) said: "He does not need to wait until the time of prayer. The instruction was given [to pray at specific times] only out of concern for public visibility [to avoid attracting undue attention]."
